name: UTAC Domain Covariates - System Property Predictors for β-Heterogeneity
source: Expert estimates based on system architecture and domain knowledge
description: System-level covariates hypothesized to predict β-parameter heterogeneity in UTAC framework. Used for meta-regression to test mechanistic theories of why different domains exhibit different β-attractors.
provenance: Covariate values estimated from domain knowledge, literature review, and theoretical considerations. See docs/appendix_field_types.md for estimation methodology. Domain identifiers match beta_estimates.csv for paired analysis.

variables.name: domain
variables.description: Domain identifier. Must match beta_estimates.csv exactly for meta-regression.

variables.name: C_eff
variables.description: Effective coupling strength. Measures interaction intensity between system components.
variables.estimation_method: Expert assessment based on: network connectivity, interaction range, feedback strength
variables.hypothesis: Higher C_eff → Higher β (stronger resistance to threshold crossing)

variables.name: D_eff
variables.description: Effective dimensionality. Represents degrees of freedom or system complexity.
variables.estimation_method: Based on: parameter count, network size, component diversity
variables.hypothesis: Higher D_eff (d≥4) → β approaches mean-field RG fixed point (β≈4.2)

variables.name: SNR
variables.description: Signal-to-noise ratio. Ratio of coherent forcing to stochastic fluctuations.
variables.estimation_method: Coherent forcing amplitude / thermal/environmental noise amplitude
variables.hypothesis: Higher SNR → Sharper transitions (higher β), lower noise → less smearing

variables.name: Memory
variables.description: Memory/hysteresis measure. Quantifies path-dependence and irreversibility.
variables.estimation_method: Based on: hysteresis width, bistability strength, history dependence
variables.hypothesis: Higher Memory → Associated with higher β in bistable systems

variables.name: Theta_dot
variables.description: Rate of threshold change. Measures adaptive/evolutionary dynamics of Θ itself.
variables.estimation_method: dΘ/dt normalized by system timescale. Captures threshold adaptation.
variables.hypothesis: Exploratory covariate; may capture moving-target dynamics

rg_derivation.prediction: β increases with C_eff and SNR

mean_field_regime.prediction: β converges to RG fixed point ≈ 4.21 (≈ Φ³)
mean_field_regime.observed: Informational systems (LLMs, Markets) with high D_eff cluster at β ≈ 4.5

estimation_methodology.validation: Cross-check against empirical β-values in beta_estimates.csv
estimation_methodology.uncertainty: Covariate estimates are inherently subjective. Meta-regression R² indicates explanatory power.
estimation_methodology.iterative_refinement: Covariates may be refined as more systems are added and patterns emerge

meta_regression_usage.expected_output: Coefficients, R², residual plots, covariate importance rankings

usage_notes: Covariates are ESTIMATES, not measured quantities
Domain identifiers must match beta_estimates.csv exactly
Missing covariates (NA) will be excluded from regression
See docs/appendix_field_types.md for covariate estimation guidance
Meta-regression tests mechanistic hypotheses (J/T, dimensionality, etc.)
Low meta-regression R² suggests missing covariates or complex interactions

quality_control.range_checks: All covariates within specified ranges [0,1] or [2,1000]
quality_control.domain_matching: All domains in beta_estimates.csv have covariate entries
quality_control.expert_review: Covariate estimates reviewed by domain experts where possible

citations: See beta_estimates.csv metadata for system-specific references
